content.title: 2025 New York City Marathon: Preview, full schedule and how to watch the action live
content.text: Several Olympic marathon stars including Eliud Kipchoge, Sifan Hassan and Hellen Obiri will compete on Sunday, 2 November. Find out everything you need to know about the race below.By Evelyn Watta 27 October 2025 11:08 GMT+06 min readThe final World Marathon Major of 2025 is set to be a classic, with Olympic champions Eliud Kipchoge of Kenya and Dutchwoman Sifan Hassan set to make their New York City Marathon debuts on Sunday, 2 November. Elsewhere in a stacked field, Hassan's Paris 2024 rivals, Hellen Obiri, the Kenyan bronze medallist, and compatriot Sharon Lokedi, who was fourth, will also be hungry to win the women's race. On the men’s side, Kipchoge will face Dutch defending champion Abdi Nageeye, and compatriots Evans Chebet and Albert Korir - both former New York City Marathon champions. Even more interest has been sparked by the late addition of Kenenisa Bekele of Ethiopia. Discover all the key information for the race below, including the schedule and where to watch the 2025 New York City Marathon. Eliud Kipchoge exclusive: "I have nothing more to prove" The mindset behind Sifan Hassan's historic treble at Paris 2024: “I already got what I wanted, I wanted a challenge” Athletes to watch at the 2025 New York City Marathon Kipchoge and Hassan, two of the most prominent figures in marathon racing, are poised to demonstrate their exceptional abilities as the fastest in their respective fields. That's just two months after both competing at the Sydney Marathon. In a break from the norm, Kipchoge will run his third marathon in the same year. Since his debut in 2013, the Kenyan legend has only raced twice in a year at most. But with nothing more to prove as the greatest marathoner, he is now ticking off personal running goals. In a couple of days, he will have competed at every World Marathon Major. “[I felt] this is the best time to line up at the start of the New York Marathon, reason being I felt that I want to be [among] the big crowd of runners that break their records in the best course ever,” he said on Set the Pace, the official podcast of the New York Road Runners. “I still feel pressure, I still feel tense, which shows that I am ready… in New York at the starting line I will still feel tense. I still train competitively, run competitively and hope to finish in a good way and leave my footprints in New York.”Chebet, who in 2022 became the third man to win both the New York City and Boston marathons, will provide a stern test for Kipchoge. The other prominent Kenyan is 2021 winner Korir, who is aiming for a fourth podium finish at the Big Apple. Kipchoge's longtime track rival, Bekele, heads back to New York after his last race there in 2021, when he finished sixth. In his fourth Olympic appearance at Paris 2024, the Ethiopian three-time Olympic champion placed 39th, with Kipchoge failing to finish a race for the first time in his career. Nageeye, the Tokyo 2020 Olympic marathon silver medallist, returns to defend his title, with Benson Kipruto, third at Paris 2024 and last year’s London Marathon champion Alexander Mutiso also competing. The new world marathon champion from Tokyo, Alphonce Simbu, will also be in New York, while Abbabiya Simbassa, an Ethiopian-born athlete making his third marathon appearance, is one of the best U.S. athletes in the field.The Great Sifan Hassan | Athletics | Olympic Games Paris 2024The other Dutch runner expected to shine in New York City is women's star Hassan, who made history at last year’s Olympics, medalling in the 5000m, 10,000m and the marathon. Just 62 days after an epic 2:20 run in Sydney, she will chase a fifth win in seven career marathons. On Staten Island, she will face off against three Kenyans who have previously won the New York City Marathon: Lokedi [2022], Obiri [2023], and Sheila Chepkirui [2024]. She wants to wrap up her season on a high, if only she can get past her usual pre-race anxiety. “The fear [I normally experience] shows that I care about that thing”, she said of the fear she experiences at the start of most of her races. “Looking back, I was more scared of starting the 1500m than the 800m because I cared about the 1500m more. And now I think I am scared of the marathon because deep down I care so much, and luckily, I get away with wins.” Two-time Olympian Emily Sisson, who is just fresh from winning the Boston 10k, will finally make her debut in one of the world's most populous cities. She is the USA's fastest-ever marathon runner. Tokyo Olympic marathon bronze medallist Molly Seidel, is another of the top locals to keep an eye on. The defending champions in the wheelchair divisions, Daniel Romanchuk and Susannah Scaroni, will also feature in this year’s race.2025 New York City Marathon schedule Sunday, 2 November The New York City Marathon has drawn over 55,000 participants, who will run through the five boroughs that make up the city. The race begins at Staten Island at 8:00am with men’s wheelchair races, with the elites set to start at 9:05am. The finishing line is in Central Park. 2025 New York City Marathon Start times: All times local time EST (UTC -5h). 8:00 a.m.: Marathon Wheelchair start (men) 8:02 a.m.: Marathon Wheelchair start (women) 8:22 a.m.: Marathon Pushrim and Handcycle start 8:35 a.m.: Elite women 9:05 a.m.: Elite men 9:10 a.m.: Wave 1 start 9:45 a.m.: Wave 2 start 10:20 a.m.: Wave 3 start 10:45 a.m.: Wave 4 start 11:30 a.m.: Wave 5 start How to watch the 2025 New York City Marathon In the U.S., viewers can follow the race on ESPN2 and on the ESPN App. ESPN3 will provide live coverage in Spanish. NBC 5 Chicago and Telemundo Chicago will provide live coverage in English and Spanish from 7 a.m. – 11 a.m. (U.S. Central Time). In New York, the race will air on ABC7/WABC-TV. International viewers can follow the race via various global broadcast partners, including ESPN International (South America, Central America, Mexico, and the Caribbean), Eurosport (Europe, Southeast Asia, India), Fox Sports/Kayo (Australia), L’Equipe (France), RAI (Italy), SMG Sports (China), SuperSport (Sub-Saharan Africa), TSN (Canada), and TVE/Tv3 (Spain).Add to your favourites Sign-up for free and you will be able to receive Olympic news tailored to your interests.
